title: Supersonic Transport Open Research Models and Impact on Environment
summary:
Research and development in the field of aviation is constantly striving to make aircraft more efficient and faster, more climate-friendly and quieter. Accordingly, new propulsion concepts and aircraft configurations are constantly being developed and measured. However, due to the large number of different configurations and the enormous costs involved, it would not be possible to first build and test every aircraft and then examine its noise impact on the population in the vicinity of existing airports. For this reason, we use the method known as auralization. Based on calculations and measurements in the wind tunnel, the noise of modern aircraft configurations is made artificially audible - well before the market launch of these aircraft. The aim of this study is to gain an impression of how people perceive and assess the noise of modern aircraft configurations.
The results of this study can help to support the development of new aircraft configurations, identify particularly unpleasant sounding configurations and improve them. Furthermore, the results of this and other studies can serve international regulatory bodies such as EASA (European Union Aviation Safety Agency) as a basis for deriving noise certification and noise protection regulations.
conditions: Aircraft noise pollution from an SST-Airliner and a subsonic conventional A320 commercial aircraft

interventions.name:
All subjects are presented with 54 target sounds via a computer with closed headphones
The sounds presented are the sounds of:
- a subsonic conventional passenger airliner (A 320)
- a Super Sonic Transport Airliner (large passenger aircraft)
- a Super Sonic Transport business jet

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Signed declarations of consent for data protection (for subject selection and for conducting the study), the subject contract and the subject consent form must be available
- Sufficient knowledge of the German language
- age-appropriate normal hearing in the frequency range 125 - 8000 Hz
Exclusion criteria:
- Hearing loss in the audiogram: i.e. the hearing thresholds in the better ear are higher than the 10th percentile of the gender- and age-specific hearing thresholds in ISO 7029 (2017)
- Wearing a hearing aid
- Hearing disorders (tinnitus with severity > 2, sudden hearing loss within the last 10 years)
- any other condition which, in the opinion of the doctors conducting the test, makes the subject unsuitable
- any medication with an influence on the test parameters or consumption of stimulants and drugs with an influence on the test parameters, e.g. drug consumption, increased alcohol consumption and nicotine consumption that does not allow abstinence for at least 10 hours
- persons without legal capacity and persons with limited legal capacity
- do not speak German
